summary: A solid active-passive multi-region DR design with explicit write-authority leasing/fencing, guarded promotion gates, and an idempotent failover workflow driven by a small control plane. It’s largely production-plausible and operationally minded (monitoring, drills, audit trail), but some key scale and edge-case details (Postgres cross-region replication at high write volume, DNS cutover realities, and non-DB state reconciliation) need more rigor.
strengths: Clear split-brain prevention via external lease + fencing token and explicit failover state machine with auditability
Practical operational focus: tiered RPO gates, progressive traffic shifting with rollback, dependency-aware health checks, and regular DR drills
weaknesses: Postgres physical streaming replication and promotion at 10TB/high write rates needs deeper treatment (lag/backlog behavior, failover correctness under partitions, and resync after region return)

DNS/GTM-only failover can be slow/probabilistic; design under-specifies handling of mixed-traffic windows and reconciliation of non-DB state (queues, caches, search/indexes, object storage) during/after cutover
